one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly ignored yt-dlp's explicit instruction to use cookie-based authentication (shown at every download attempt from step 4 onward), then abandoned the task by writing a failure-narrative file instead of the required move list.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: yt-dlp explicitly outputs 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. Use --cookies-from-browser or --cookies for the authentication.' The agent sees this message but at step 5 immediately retries with different unauthenticated parameters instead of following the cookie-auth instruction.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14: After chromium-browser installation completes (step 13), the agent abandons the cookie-extraction path entirely and pivots to curl/wget/Python HTTP probing. This is the last moment where using 'yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chromium' was feasible; after step 14 the agent never returns to this approach and subsequently pursues only ineffective HTML scraping and a failure narrative.
t_surface_evidence: Step 4: The authentication error 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot' is the first explicit observable failure signal returned by yt-dlp.
trigger_explanation: At step 4, yt-dlp clearly states the required fix (use --cookies-from-browser or --cookies), but the agent ignores this and continues with five more unauthenticated yt-dlp variants (steps 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 20, 25) and HTML scraping (steps 17-24) — the same auth-blocked path — rather than following the explicit tool guidance.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 20, 25 all produce the identical 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot' error. The agent repeatedly issues yt-dlp commands without cookies, generating the same error each time — a clear pattern of repeated failure before t_commit at step 14.
